title: 帯広「藤丸パーク」がイベント連発　百貨店後継開業までにぎわい創出
extracted_text:
北海道帯広市の藤丸パークが25日、今年の営業を始めた。閉店した百貨店の後継施設ができるまでの「つなぎ」店舗で、冬季休業を経た2年目はイベント会場としての利用を促進。街中再生を願う住民が当事者となってにぎわいの場を作る。

藤丸パークは特異な経緯で始まった。122年の歴史を持つ百貨店「藤丸」が閉店したのが2023年1月。各地の百貨店跡地は商業利用が見込めずマンションや、複雑な権利関係から放置される例が目立つ。

救世主となったのが事業再生に関わるスタートアップのそら（帯広市）と、自動車販売の村松ホールディングス（HD、同）だ。いずれも移住者が設立した会社で権利関係を調整。帯広市が危険な建物を除去する国の補助制度と、企業版ふるさと納税による10億円の寄付で約20億円の解体費のほぼ全額をまかない、既に工事が始まっている。

後継施設は2030年開業を目指すが、それまでにぎわいを維持しようと25年7月にオープンしたのが藤丸パーク。企業や市民の3億円の寄付金を使い、帯広信用金庫の土地3200平方メートルを使い飲食店など仮設4店と広場でスタートした。

「驚くほど人通りが少ない街だが、昨年の実績はまずます」と運営する藤丸（同）の山中良助社長は語る。三菱UFJ銀行から母校の京都大学アメリカンフットボール部コーチを経てそらに入社した移住者だ。昨年は約4カ月間の営業で6万人を集客し、6000万円を売り上げた。

人口16万人の帯広市では長崎屋も閉店し中心部の大型商業施設がゼロに。通行量はピーク時の10分の1だが、「楽しいイベントを開けば来てくれる」といい、餃子フェスには1日500〜600人が集まったという。日ごろの街中をみていると大盛況だ。

そこで、今年の柱に掲げたのが、「イベントに使ってもらい関係人口を増やすこと」。島根県のキャンプ場などで集客した実績を持つ長谷川貴彦ディレクターを起用。長谷川氏は「思い出のある藤丸で新たなストーリーを作りたい人を巻き込もう」とイベントを仕込んできた。

5月に開く「十勝ととのうフェス」は、サウナトラックを所有する愛好家によるイベント。8月に開く「モール温泉ぶっかけ祭り」は地元人気ラーメン店の店主が屋外をいかして盛り上げたいと提案した。ベトナムフェスは地元高校教師が在住ベトナム人との交流を図ろうと、雇用企業に声をかけて準備中という。

藤丸パークは敷地の大部分が広場で雨風に弱いが、「アウトドアと考えてイベントを開けばいい」と長谷川氏。期間中40〜45件のイベントを開きにぎわいを作る考えだ。

ペットフードも扱う荻野興業（北海道大樹町）の荻野ひとみ専務はペット愛好家と5月にイベントを開く。「（売り上げ歩合の）出店料はちょっと高いが、外から来た人が頑張っている。地元民として盛り上げたい」と初めて企画した。「祖母が『藤丸さん』と呼び、私も通った特別な場所。年齢を問わず集まれるといい」と期待する。

資材高騰などで商業施設には不透明感もある。帯広商工会議所の川田章博会頭は「実際に解体を始めるなど関係者には感謝している」としつつ「先行きがはっきりしない」と語る。ただ、施設ありきの再開発により各地で破綻が相次いだ。パークでにぎわいが生まれれば、中心市街地活性化の新たな手法になる。

（帯広支局長　浅山章）
translated_text:
Fujimaru Park in Obihiro, Hokkaido, opened for the year on the 25th. Serving as an interim facility until the successor to the closed department store is completed, this second year following a winter closure will focus on promoting the space as an event venue. Local residents who hope for downtown revitalization are taking the initiative to create a lively gathering place.

Fujimaru Park had an unusual path to opening. The department store Fujimaru, which operated for 122 years, closed in January 2023. Across Japan, former department store sites tend to be converted to condominiums or simply left abandoned due to complex ownership issues.

The unlikely saviors were startup Sora, involved in business revitalization, and automotive dealer Muraoka Holdings—both based in Obihiro. Both companies were founded by newcomers to the area who negotiated the ownership complexities. Using a state subsidy program for removing hazardous structures, combined with 1 billion yen in corporate-local tax donations, the city covered nearly all of the approximately 2 billion yen demolition costs. Construction has already begun.

The successor facility is targeting a 2030 opening. To maintain momentum until then, Fujimaru Park opened in July 2025. With 300 million yen in donations from businesses and citizens, and utilizing land spanning 3,200 square meters from Obihiro Shinkin Bank, it launched with four temporary food and beverage establishments and a large open plaza.

"The city has surprisingly little foot traffic, but last year's results were decent," says President Yamanaka Ryosuke of Fujimaru, which operates the park. A newcomer who joined from Sora after working as a coach for Kyoto University's American football team, sponsored by Mitsubishi UFJ Bank. Last year, roughly four months of operation drew 60,000 visitors and generated 60 million yen in sales.

Obihiro, with a population of 160,000, has also seen Nagasakioya close, leaving zero large commercial facilities in the central area. Foot traffic has dropped to a tenth of its peak, but "when we hold fun events, people come," reports that the Gyoza Festival attracted 500 to 600 people per day.

This year, the park's key strategy is "using events to increase the related population." Director Hasegawa Takahiko, with a track record attracting visitors at campsites in Shimane Prefecture, was brought on. Hasegawa has been orchestrating events to involve people who want to create new stories at Fujimaru.

The "Tokachi Relaxation Festival" in May will feature a sauna truck event organized by enthusiasts. The "Mall Onsen Festival" in August was proposed by a popular local ramen shop owner who wants to draw crowds outdoors. A Vietnamese Festival is being organized by a local high school teacher working with Vietnamese residents in the area, coordinating with their employers.

While most of the site is an open plaza vulnerable to rain and wind, "we just need to think outdoors and hold events," says Hasegawa. The plan is to host 40 to 45 events during the season to generate buzz.

Ogino Hitomi, an executive director at Ogino Kogyo in Daiki town, Hokkaido—which also handles pet food—is organizing an event in May with pet enthusiasts. "The booth fees are a bit high, but people from outside are really trying hard. As a local, I want to help boost the energy," she says of her first event. "My grandmother called it 'Fujimaru-san,' and I shopped there too. It was a special place. I hope people of all ages can gather there."

While material costs and other uncertainties cloud the outlook for commercial facilities, Obihiro Chamber of Commerce President Kawada Akira says, "We are grateful to those actually beginning demolition." However, development schemes centered on new facilities have repeatedly failed across the country. If Fujimaru Park succeeds in generating buzz, it could become a new model for central district revitalization.

(Reporter: Asayama Akira, Obihiro Bureau)
title_en: Fujimaru Park in Obihiro Launches Series of Events to Build Momentum Until New Department Store Opens
